Subject: Exploring move to annual prepay — ramp, rollback & true-up options

Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick chat last week. We're evaluating moving Soteria from our current monthly usage billing to an annual prepay to simplify forecasting and secure better unit economics. Before we loop procurement, a few clarifying questions so we can compare apples-to-apples: 

- Do you offer a staged ramp (we expect 40% growth next 12 months) where discounts scale with committed spend, or is discounting flat for the term?
- Procurement is concerned about locking in full spend immediately. Is there a rollback or exit mechanism if adoption is below agreed ramp milestones?
- How do you handle monthly true-ups if we over/under-use versus our committed prepay?
- Any onboarding or SLA credits you can provide for a 1-year vs 2-year commitment?

I've attached our Q3 usage so you can model different commitment tiers (usage_report_q3.csv). Would appreciate a short options memo and a sample term sheet we can send to procurement. Happy to schedule a call if it's easier.

Best,
Ava

Hi Ava — great to hear from you and thanks for the data. Internal cc: Marissa to align on commercial flexibility. Below are three pragmatic options that map to common procurement asks. I've kept the language operational so you can paste into your procurement packet.

Option A — 12-month prepay (conservative)
- Commitment: 12 months, prepay of 100% of first-year committed spend.
- Discount: 20% off list usage rates.
- Ramp guardrail: Quarterly true-up. If actual monthly usage falls below 70% of the trailing 3-month ramp target for a quarter, we will issue a one-time credit equal to the shortfall multiplied by 25% as a protective refund.
- Rollback: 90-day rollback window in first 6 months with a 10% early termination fee on remaining prepay.
- SLA/onboarding: One-time onboarding credit of $8k and 30-day premium onboarding support.

Option B — 24-month prepay (growth-weighted)
- Commitment: 24 months, staged prepay: 50% upfront year 1, 50% upfront year 2.
- Discount: 30% off list usage rates, with step-up discount bands if 12-month avg usage >130% of committed levels.
- Ramp: Month-by-month true-up with netting; if usage exceeds commitment we credit future months or issue an invoice (your preference).
- Rollback: 60-day rollback in first 4 months; reduced termination fee (5%) and obligation to true-up for first 90 days' over-use.
- SLA/onboarding: $15k onboarding credit + two guaranteed dedicated onboarding sessions.

Option C — Pilot-to-prepay (low friction)
- 6-month pilot with monthly invoicing, option to convert to 12 or 24-month prepay at any time with retroactive credit for pilot spend toward committed amount.
- Conversion incentive: 10% credit on pilot spend when converting within 30 days.

Monthly true-up mechanics (how it works)
- We run a monthly usage reconciliation. Overages beyond committed tier are applied to next month's credits or invoiced. Underuse triggers the quarterly shortfall protection described above depending on the selected option.

Next steps
- If any of these look viable I can draft a concise term sheet (redlineable) and a DocuSign packet for procurement. Would you prefer "credit toward next invoice" or "immediate invoice" for overages?

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Rishi,

Thanks — that framing is super helpful. Procurement prefers:

- Month-by-month true-up applied as a credit to the following invoice (keeps our AP clean).
- A rollback that exists but with a limited financial penalty — the 60-day rollback on the 24-month sounds like a reasonable baseline, but can we add a condition that rollback is not permitted after 6 months unless both parties agree?
- We want KPI-tied discount enhancements: if Soteria hits a defined usage growth curve (I can share a target ramp) you provide an additional 5% rebate at true-up for that quarter.

Two asks from procurement side before we route to legal:
1) Please send a short redlined term sheet (one page) with clear definitions: committed units, true-up cadence, rollback window, termination fees.
2) Include a sample DocuSign envelope so procurement can validate signing workflow (we use a mix of CFO + procurement).

Can Marissa also confirm whether onboarding credits affect T&Cs or are simply one-time bill credits?

Thanks,
Ava
